certifications.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
certifications.status: Active. CLF-C02 is the current version. No successor announced as of 30 Sep 2026 (see 'unverified' - this was not checked against the AWS 'Coming Soon to AWS Certification' page).
certifications.questionCount: 65 total (50 scored + 15 unscored); multiple choice and multiple response
certifications.passingScore: 700 of 100-1,000 scaled (compensatory - no per-domain pass requirement)
certifications.recommendedExperience: Up to 6 months of exposure to AWS Cloud design, implementation and/or operations. No coding, architecture design, troubleshooting, implementation or load testing expected.

domains.name: Domain 1: Cloud Concepts
domains.covers: Benefits of the AWS Cloud, AWS Cloud design principles, migration benefits and strategies (AWS CAF, migration strategies), and cloud economics (fixed vs variable cost, right-sizing, automation, managed-service cost benefit)

domains.name: Domain 2: Security and Compliance
domains.covers: AWS shared responsibility model, security/governance/compliance concepts (Artifact, compliance programs, GuardDuty, Inspector, Shield, WAF), IAM access management (root account, users, groups, roles, policies, MFA, IAM Identity Center), and security support resources (Trusted Advisor, Security Hub, KMS)

domains.name: Domain 3: Cloud Technology and Services
domains.covers: Deployment and operating methods (console, CLI, SDKs, IaC, connectivity), AWS global infrastructure (Regions, AZs, edge locations), compute (EC2, Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Elastic Beanstalk, Auto Scaling, ELB), databases (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, Redshift, ElastiCache, DMS), networking (VPC, subnets, security groups, NACLs, Route 53, CloudFront, Direct Connect, VPN), storage (S3 and storage classes, EBS, EFS, FSx, Storage Gateway, AWS Backup), and AI/ML, analytics and other service categories

domains.name: Domain 4: Billing, Pricing, and Support
domains.covers: Pricing models (On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot, dedicated hosts, data transfer), billing and cost management tools (Billing Console, Cost Explorer, Budgets, Cost and Usage Report, Pricing Calculator, Organizations consolidated billing, cost allocation tags), and support resources (Support plans, Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, Knowledge Center, Partner Network, Professional Services, Marketplace)

keyServices: AWS IAM and IAM Identity Center
AWS Cost Explorer / AWS Budgets / AWS Pricing Calculator
Elastic Load Balancing / EC2 Auto Scaling

certifications.name: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
certifications.status: Active. GA since 2024 and still the current version as of 30 Sep 2026.
certifications.questionCount: 65 total (50 scored + 15 unscored); multiple choice, multiple response, ordering and matching. This is the only exam in the foundational/associate set that uses ordering and matching.
certifications.recommendedExperience: Up to 6 months of exposure to AI/ML technologies on AWS. The candidate USES rather than BUILDS AI/ML solutions. Familiarity with core AWS services (EC2, S3, Lambda, Bedrock, SageMaker AI), the shared responsibility model, IAM and AWS pricing models. Model development, feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning and pipeline building are out of scope.

domains.name: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML
domains.covers: AI/ML/deep-learning terminology (inferencing, model, training data, labelled vs unlabelled), supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement learning, practical use cases and when AI is not appropriate, and the ML development lifecycle with MLOps concepts and metrics

domains.name: Domain 2: Fundamentals of Generative AI
domains.covers: Foundation-model concepts (tokens, embeddings, vectors, chunking, transformers, prompt engineering, diffusion, multimodal), GenAI use cases and limitations (hallucination, nondeterminism, interpretability), and AWS infrastructure for GenAI (Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Q, PartyRock) plus cost tradeoffs

domains.name: Domain 3: Applications of Foundation Models
domains.covers: Design considerations for FM applications (model selection, inference parameters such as temperature and output length, RAG and vector stores - OpenSearch Service, Aurora pgvector, Neptune, DocumentDB, RDS for PostgreSQL), prompt-engineering techniques (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought) and risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking), plus training/fine-tuning approaches and evaluation (ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, human evaluation)

domains.name: Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI
domains.covers: Responsible AI dimensions - bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity; tools such as Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker Clarify; dataset bias and its effects; and transparency mechanisms including AWS AI Service Cards and model cards, and the interpretability/performance tradeoff

domains.name: Domain 5: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
domains.covers: Securing AI systems (IAM roles and policies, encryption, Amazon Macie, PrivateLink, source citation and data lineage, data-quality controls) and governance/compliance for AI systems (ISO, SOC, algorithm accountability) using AWS Config, Inspector, Audit Manager, Artifact, CloudTrail and Trusted Advisor

keyServices: Amazon SageMaker AI (JumpStart, Clarify, Model Cards, Data Wrangler, Ground Truth)
AWS CloudTrail / AWS Config / AWS Audit Manager

certifications.recommendedExperience: A business professional who evaluates, champions or scales AI initiatives - product/program managers, sales, line-of-business managers, consultants, marketers, business analysts. Works alongside technical teams but does not build AI solutions. No coding or hands-on AWS implementation required. Baseline of roughly 6 months working with or alongside teams adopting AI.

domains.name: Domain 1: AI Fundamentals and Literacy
domains.covers: Applying foundational AI/ML/GenAI concepts and terminology to business contexts, selecting AI solution types against business requirements and constraints, and using GenAI techniques (prompt engineering, model adaptation) to achieve business outcomes

domains.name: Domain 2: AI Strategy and Business Value Creation
domains.covers: Developing and prioritising AI strategies aligned to organisational objectives, measuring AI business value with KPIs, ROI frameworks and baseline metrics, and positioning AI initiatives for competitive advantage and business-model transformation, including build-buy-partner decisions and AWS pricing/cost tooling at a business level

domains.name: Domain 3: AI Governance and Responsible AI Leadership
domains.covers: Applying responsible AI principles to business decisions involving tradeoffs, establishing governance structures and regulatory compliance for AI initiatives, and identifying enterprise AI risks and directing mitigation strategies

domains.name: Domain 4: Business Readiness, Leadership, and AI Transformation
domains.covers: Assessing organisational AI readiness and maturity across people, process, technology and governance; evaluating data and infrastructure foundations; leading enterprise change management and workforce capability building; and scaling AI from pilots to enterprise-wide deployment

Amazon SageMaker AI (managed vs custom ML decisions)
AWS Well-Architected Framework - Responsible AI Lens

The last day to take the current exam (DVA-C02) is December 1, 2026.' The AWS September 2026 blog gives the last day as 30 November 2026 with DVA-C03 GA on 1 December 2026 - the two official sources differ by one day, so book on or before 30 November 2026 to be safe. Superseded by DVA-C03.

The guide also carries an 'Emerging topics' section of UNSCORED pretest questions on AI-assisted development, AI security risks, AI-generated tests, AI in CI/CD, AI error analysis and AI-driven optimisation - these do not affect your score but signal where DVA-C03 is heading.
certifications.recommendedExperience: 1 or more years of hands-on experience developing and maintaining applications using AWS services, proficiency in at least one high-level programming language, understanding of application lifecycle management, and ability to use a CI/CD pipeline to deploy on AWS. Designing architectures, designing CI/CD pipelines, IAM administration, server/OS administration and network design are out of scope.

domains.name: Domain 1: Development with AWS Services
domains.covers: Writing code for applications hosted on AWS (Lambda handlers, event-driven and stateless/idempotent design, SDKs, retries and exponential backoff), developing code for AWS Lambda, and using data stores in application development (DynamoDB data modelling and queries, S3, RDS, ElastiCache, caching and TTL, serialization)

domains.name: Domain 2: Security
domains.covers: Authentication and authorization for applications and AWS services (Cognito user and identity pools, IAM roles and policies, resource policies, federated access, token-based auth), encryption using AWS services (KMS keys, envelope encryption, client- vs server-side, TLS/ACM), and managing sensitive data in application code (Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store, rotation, keeping secrets out of code and logs)

domains.name: Domain 3: Deployment
domains.covers: Preparing application artifacts (packaging, Lambda layers, container images to ECR, environment variables and configuration), testing in development environments, automating deployment testing, and deploying with AWS CI/CD services (CodePipeline, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CloudFormation, SAM, CDK, Elastic Beanstalk) using blue/green, canary, rolling and all-at-once strategies

domains.name: Domain 4: Troubleshooting and Optimization
domains.covers: Root cause analysis (CloudWatch Logs and Logs Insights, metrics and alarms, X-Ray traces and service map, CloudTrail, HTTP error codes, SDK exceptions), instrumenting code for observability (structured logging, custom metrics, embedded metric format, distributed tracing), and optimizing applications (Lambda memory/concurrency and provisioned concurrency, caching with ElastiCache/CloudFront/API Gateway, DynamoDB capacity tuning)

keyServices: AWS Secrets Manager / AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
Amazon SQS / SNS / EventBridge / AWS Step Functions
AWS CloudFormation / AWS SAM / AWS CDK
Amazon ECS / Amazon ECR / AWS Fargate
Amazon CloudWatch (Logs, Logs Insights, metrics, alarms)

certifications.name: AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate
certifications.status: Active. Current as of 30 Sep 2026; no successor announced (see 'unverified' - not checked against the AWS 'Coming Soon' page). The exam guide carries a Revisions section, and AWS publishes guide revisions at least one month before they reach the live exam. The target-candidate description now includes 'general concepts of vectors'.
certifications.questionCount: 65 total (50 scored + 15 unscored); multiple choice and multiple response
certifications.recommendedExperience: The equivalent of 2-3 years of data engineering experience plus at least 1-2 years of hands-on AWS experience. Should understand the effects of volume, variety and velocity on ingestion, transformation, modelling, security, governance, privacy, schema design and data store design; know Git, data lakes, SQL, general networking/storage/compute and vector concepts. ML training/inference and drawing business conclusions are out of scope.

domains.name: Domain 1: Data Ingestion and Transformation
domains.covers: Data ingestion (streaming vs batch, Kinesis Data Streams, Data Firehose, MSK, DynamoDB Streams, throughput and replayability), transforming and processing data (Glue ETL and Spark, EMR, Lambda, container-based processing, conversion to Parquet/ORC), orchestrating pipelines (Step Functions, MWAA/Airflow, EventBridge, Glue workflows), and programming concepts (CI/CD for pipelines, SQL, IaC, code optimization)

domains.name: Domain 2: Data Store Management
domains.covers: Choosing a data store (S3 and storage classes, Redshift, DynamoDB, RDS/Aurora, DocumentDB, Keyspaces, Neptune), cataloguing systems (Glue Data Catalog, crawlers, schema discovery, Hive metastore), data lifecycle (S3 lifecycle and Intelligent-Tiering, hot/warm/cold tiering, retention, Redshift/Aurora backups), and data models and schema evolution (star/snowflake schemas, partitioning, compression, indexing, Lake Formation)

domains.name: Domain 3: Data Operations and Support
domains.covers: Automating data processing (Glue, Lambda, EventBridge, SDKs, MWAA), analysing data (Athena, Redshift and Redshift Spectrum, EMR, OpenSearch Service, QuickSight), maintaining and monitoring pipelines (CloudWatch metrics, logs and alarms, CloudTrail, Glue job metrics, cost and performance troubleshooting), and ensuring data quality (Glue Data Quality, DataBrew, completeness, consistency, profiling, anomaly detection)

domains.name: Domain 4: Data Security and Governance
domains.covers: Authentication and authorization (IAM roles and policies, Lake Formation permissions, IAM Identity Center, cross-account access), encryption and masking (KMS, encryption at rest and in transit, client-side, masking and anonymization), preparing logs for audit (CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs, Glue and Redshift logging, Macie, CloudTrail Lake), and data privacy and governance (PII handling, Macie, data sharing, compliance, cross-Region considerations)

keyServices: AWS Glue (ETL, Data Catalog, crawlers, DataBrew, Data Quality)
Amazon S3 (storage classes, lifecycle, S3 Select)
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka)
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA)
AWS KMS / AWS IAM / Amazon Macie

certifications.name: AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer - Associate
certifications.status: Active. This certification REPLACED AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate: the exam was renamed effective 30 September 2025 and the code moved from SOA-C02 to SOA-C03. It is a rename plus content update, not a new certification - the guide contains a 'Comparison of SOA-C02 and SOA-C03' section confirming SOA-C02 ran to 29 Sep 2025 and SOA-C03 from 30 Sep 2025, with six domains collapsing to five (the old Domain 6, Cost and Performance Optimization, folded into Task 1.3). The docs URL slug is still '.../sysops-administrator-associate-03/...', which is expected for a rename. Holders of the old SysOps Administrator - Associate credential keep it valid for 3 years from the date earned and need not retake. Simplified Chinese and Korean versions retire after 19 November 2026. Note on hands-on labs: NEITHER SOA-C02 (since March 2023) NOR SOA-C03 includes exam labs - labs were removed from SOA-C02 in March 2023, well before SOA-C03 existed, so SOA-C03 did not 'drop' them.
certifications.questionCount: 65 total (50 scored + 15 unscored); multiple choice and multiple response only
certifications.recommendedExperience: 1 year of experience with deployment, management, troubleshooting, networking and security on AWS, plus at least 1 year in a related operations role such as system administrator. Should know monitoring/logging/troubleshooting, networking concepts (DNS, TCP/IP, firewalls), at least one scripting language and one major OS, containerization and orchestration basics, and CI/CD and Git. Designing distributed architectures, designing CI/CD pipelines, designing hybrid/multi-VPC networking, software development, defining security/compliance/governance requirements, capacity planning and cost/TCO analysis are out of scope.

domains.name: Content Domain 1: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
domains.covers: Implementing metrics, alarms and filters with CloudWatch; collecting, analysing and retaining logs (CloudWatch Logs, Logs Insights, CloudTrail); remediating issues based on monitoring and availability data; and optimising performance of compute, storage, database and network resources

domains.name: Content Domain 2: Reliability and Business Continuity
domains.covers: Scalability and elasticity (EC2 Auto Scaling, ELB, caching), high availability and resilient environments (Multi-AZ, Route 53 health checks and routing, decoupled architectures), and backup/restore and disaster recovery (AWS Backup, snapshots, RDS/Aurora backups, S3 versioning and replication, RTO/RPO)

domains.name: Content Domain 3: Deployment, Provisioning, and Automation
domains.covers: Provisioning and maintaining cloud resources (AMIs, CloudFormation templates and StackSets, Systems Manager, Elastic Beanstalk, container provisioning) and automating manual or repeatable processes (Systems Manager Automation and Run Command, Lambda, EventBridge rules, CLI/SDK scripting, patch management)

domains.name: Content Domain 4: Security and Compliance
domains.covers: Implementing and managing security and compliance policies (IAM users/groups/roles/policies, Organizations SCPs, IAM Identity Center, cross-account access, AWS Config rules, Security Hub, GuardDuty, Inspector, Audit Manager) and data/infrastructure protection (KMS encryption at rest and in transit, Secrets Manager, ACM, Macie, Shield, WAF)

domains.name: Content Domain 5: Networking and Content Delivery
domains.covers: Implementing networking features and connectivity (VPC subnets, route tables, security groups, NACLs, NAT gateways, VPC endpoints, Transit Gateway, peering, Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect), configuring domains, DNS and content delivery (Route 53, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, ACM), and troubleshooting connectivity (VPC Flow Logs, Reachability Analyzer, DNS resolution, ELB errors)

keyServices: Amazon CloudWatch (metrics, alarms, Logs, Logs Insights, agent)
AWS Systems Manager (Session Manager, Run Command, Patch Manager, Automation, Parameter Store)
Amazon EC2 (AMIs, instance types, placement, EBS)
EC2 Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing
Amazon VPC (route tables, security groups, NACLs, NAT, endpoints, Flow Logs, Transit Gateway, peering)
Amazon EBS / Amazon EFS / AWS Storage Gateway
AWS IAM / AWS Organizations / IAM Identity Center
AWS KMS / AWS Secrets Manager / AWS Certificate Manager
AWS Config / AWS Security Hub / Amazon GuardDuty / Amazon Inspector
AWS Trusted Advisor / AWS Health Dashboard
Amazon ECS / Amazon EKS / AWS Fargate

recertification.validYears: 3 years from the date earned, or from the date of a qualifying recertification action. Renewal adds 3 years; a maintenance action adds 1 year. Both are dated from completion, not from the old expiry date.
recertification.howToRenew: Three routes. (1) Pass the latest version of the same exam, using the 50% discount voucher that appears in your AWS Certification Account. (2) Step up - passing a higher-level exam renews the lower one (for example, Solutions Architect - Professional renews Solutions Architect - Associate; DevOps Engineer - Professional renews CloudOps Engineer - Associate). (3) For Cloud Practitioner only, complete the free AWS Cloud Quest: Recertify Cloud Practitioner activity. A credential earned before its exam retires stays valid for the full 3 years - retirement stops new issuance, it does not revoke badges - but a retired exam cannot be re-sat to renew, so plan the successor exam before expiry.
recertification.freePath: AWS Cloud Quest: Recertify Cloud Practitioner - a game-based AWS Skill Builder activity that renews AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner with no exam and no exam fee. This is the ONLY free renewal path. There is no free Skill Builder renewal for any associate, professional or specialty certification; those still require passing an exam. Any claim otherwise is wrong.

microcredentials.what: Free (since 23 April 2026 - no AWS Skill Builder subscription needed), hands-on, timed assessments run inside a provisioned live AWS environment. There are no multiple-choice questions: you are dropped into a simulated business scenario and must actually complete and troubleshoot tasks. Roughly 2 hours each, available in multiple languages, with unlimited attempts. In one line: a certification is a proctored, paid, role-based exam validating broad knowledge across a domain and valid for 3 years; a microcredential is a free hands-on lab evaluation validating one specific capability you can perform. AWS positions them as complementary, with microcredentials aligned roughly to associate-level depth. Microcredentials do NOT renew and do NOT substitute for a certification. CAUTION: the live roster shifts month to month and AWS has not clearly published validity periods or attempt limits - verify on AWS Skill Builder before relying on any fixed list.

ourRecommendedOrder.note: Our opinion, not AWS's. AWS's role cards are, among other things, marketing for exams; this ordering is optimised for capability and hiring outcomes for one specific target - DevOps at large scale from a standing start - and it deliberately skips several exams AWS sells. Total for the three exams that matter: $600 ($150 SAA-C03 + $150 SOA-C03 + $300 DOP-C02). Roughly 24 months elapsed from genuine zero, of which about 18 months is unglamorous production work and 6 months is exam preparation; anyone promising 6 months is selling a course. The real bar is not the exam: can you rebuild the production environment from an empty account using only code in git? If not, the certificate is decoration. For the record, AWS currently lists 12 certifications (Cloud Practitioner and AI Practitioner at foundational; Solutions Architect, Developer, CloudOps Engineer, Data Engineer and Machine Learning Engineer at associate; Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer at professional; Advanced Networking and Security at specialty; plus Generative AI Developer - Professional), with AWS Certified AI Business Strategist in beta in a separate Business category.

steps.why: Linux, networking (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, BGP basics), Python and git, plus a real workload you personally run - a small service with a database behind a load balancer, in your own account, that you actually pay for. Three to six months. The bill is the best teacher AWS has. Without this, every AWS exam degrades into memorising service names, which is exactly the failure mode that makes certified people useless in incidents.
steps.skipIf: You already run production workloads you personally provisioned and pay for.

steps.why: Your first and possibly only associate exam. Take it because it is the credential recruiters filter on, and because it forces breadth across VPC, IAM, storage and compute that you cannot fake later. Two to three months alongside a job.
steps.skipIf: Do not skip. This is the one exam we would keep in every version of this plan.

steps.why: Monitoring, remediation and reliability - the content DOP-C02 assumes you already have. The most skippable of the three.
steps.skipIf: You are already on call for production. Go straight to step 3.

steps.why: The part no certification path mentions. Own a CI/CD pipeline. Write CloudFormation or CDK that others depend on. Get paged at 3am and write the postmortem. DOP-C02 is written for people who have done this; sitting it before is how you get a certificate you cannot defend in an interview.
steps.skipIf: Nothing skips this. Shortening it is the single most expensive mistake on this path.

steps.why: The terminal certification for this career, and the only AWS exam whose content genuinely maps to the job: pipeline design, IaC, resilience, observability, incident response, governance automation. Roughly 150 hours, and it should feel like revision rather than learning if step 3 was real.
steps.skipIf: Do not skip if large-scale DevOps is the goal.

steps.why: AWS itself marks it optional for anyone with an IT or STEM background. It teaches vocabulary you absorb in a fortnight of real use and signals nothing to a hiring manager for a DevOps role. $100 and 30 hours better spent on step 0.
steps.skipIf: Take it only if your employer reimburses it, or you are switching from a non-technical role and need one early win.

steps.why: Excellent exam, wrong career. Solutions Architect - Professional is for people who design and sell multi-account enterprise migrations. DOP-C02 covers the operational surface; SAP mostly adds migration-strategy content you will never be paged about. (Note the version change: SAP-C02's last day is 16-17 November 2026 and SAP-C03 registration opens 27 October 2026.)
steps.skipIf: Consider it years later if you move toward platform architecture or consulting.

steps.why: Heavy overlap with SAA and DOP. Its unique content - SDK specifics, Cognito flows - is better learned by writing code than by sitting an exam. Collecting all three associates is a hobby, not a strategy. (Note the version change: DVA-C02's last day is 30 November / 1 December 2026 and DVA-C03 registration opens 27 October 2026.)
steps.skipIf: Take it only if you are moving INTO development rather than out of it.

steps.why: AWS recommends it on nearly every role card, which is a signal about AWS's priorities rather than yours. It is a foundational exam, and foundational exams do not move a DevOps career. If your platform starts hosting inference, learn Bedrock and SageMaker by running them - the operational skills transfer, the certificate does not.
steps.skipIf: Take it if an employer or client specifically asks for it.

steps.why: Retiring 31 December 2026 with no announced replacement, so any effort now has a hard expiry on its market value. The networking you need for DevOps at scale - VPC design, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, DNS, TLS - is already inside SAA and DOP.
steps.skipIf: Take it only if you are specifically becoming a hybrid-networking specialist, and only before 31 December 2026.

steps.why: The one specialty that earns its place for a large-scale DevOps lead, because at scale you own guardrails, IAM boundaries and audit evidence whether you wanted to or not. Note the code: SCS-C03, since SCS-C02 was retired on 1 December 2025.
steps.skipIf: Not yet. Take it after DOP-C02 and after you have been through a real compliance audit - roughly year 3.

SAP-C03 price ($300), duration (180 minutes) and question count (75) are assumed from SAP-C02 and are NOT published for C03. Its passing score, domain weightings, task statements and in-scope service list do not exist publicly until 27 October 2026 - anything quoting them today is fabricated.

DVA-C03 domain weightings, task statements, passing score and in-scope services are not published until registration opens on 27 October 2026. Its price, duration and question count come from the AWS September 2026 blog rather than an exam guide.

SAP-C02 last testing day: the AWS September 2026 blog says 16 November 2026; the AWS certification page says 17 November 2026. One-day conflict between two official sources, unresolved - book by 16 November.

The per-certification keyServices lists are a synthesis of each exam guide's task statements plus the linked In-Scope AWS Services appendices. The individual 'In-Scope AWS Services' subpages were not each fetched line by line. High confidence, not line-verified.
